contract: The PodcastManager episode download queue runs one download at a time in order, reports success and failure, skips known feed episodes and loses only in-memory queue state on restart.
exceptions: normal, error and edge facets are covered by the listed scenarios.
force is not applicable: the queue has no force/override operation; downloads start from the download-episodes route and the new-episode check.

The scheduled cron path (runEpisodeCheck with maxEpisodesToKeep pruning and notifications) is not asserted because it is time-scheduled and not reachable by a request; the checknew download path is asserted instead.

The queue's missing-folder re-creation, deleted-library-item mid-download and ffmpeg-succeeds-but-probe-fails branches are not asserted: they need an external folder/item deletion or a media sample that ffmpeg copies while ffprobe rejects, which a deterministic local fixture cannot provide.

invariants.contract: Requested episodes download one at a time in request order: episode_download_started and episode_download_finished follow the queue order, episode_download_queued is emitted for each waiting episode, each successful download leaves one podcast episode row with its audio file, and a pre-existing file at the target name is kept while the new episode is written with a random-id suffix.

A download whose request fails, or whose file cannot be probed after the untagged retry, emits episode_download_finished with isFinished true, failed true and a finish time, leaves no episode row and no file, and the next queued episode still downloads.

The new-episode check downloads the new feed episodes with their guid, enclosure and publication time, and a later check does not download again an episode with the same guid but a new URL nor one with the same enclosure URL but a new guid (episode identity is guid or enclosure URL).
Stopping the server during a download creates no episode row, the in-memory running and waiting downloads are gone after restart, and posting the episode again downloads it once with its audio file.
